title: Jordan church attack survivor says her cousin died before her eyes
gist: Reuters via Al-Monitor: nine people died and 40 were wounded when gunmen attacked a Greek Orthodox church funeral in Karak, Jordan; King Abdullah ordered an 'iron fist' response and attackers remain at large.

insights.claim: Gunmen attacked St George's Greek Orthodox Church in Hamoud, Karak governorate (about 120 km southwest of Amman) during a funeral, killing nine and wounding 40 in a rare attack on Jordan's Christian minority.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Security shock for a normally stable state; monitor Jordan risk premium.

insights.claim: King Abdullah, a US partner against Islamist militants, ordered security forces to respond with an 'iron fist' to what authorities called extremist terrorism.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Expect a security crackdown in Jordan.

insights.claim: Authorities are still searching for the attackers, say it is too early to link them to known groups, and no claim of responsibility has been made.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Attribution unresolved; escalation risk depends on who is responsible.
insights.locator: Authorities have said they are still searching

insights.claim: Such attacks are highly unusual in Jordan, a relatively stable Middle Eastern state, though authorities say they have foiled several Islamist plots in recent years.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Baseline stability is intact but the regional war raises spillover risk.

insights.claim: A survivor, Sahar al-Halsa, described hiding behind a pillar and seeing her cousin die; the priest's message after the attack was one of love and peace.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
